r0069: 34.  The Court therefore concludes that, when it tried and convicted the applicant, the Istanbul National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) was not an independent and impartial tribunal within the meaning of Article 6 § 1 of the Convention.
r0071: 35.  The applicant further alleged under Article 6 of the Convention that he had not been able to have the assistance of a lawyer during his police custody and, furthermore, that he had been convicted on the basis of the statements he had made to the police. In that connection, he relied on Article 6 §§ 1 and 3 (c) of the Convention.
r0073: 37.  The Court reiterates that it has already held in similar cases that a court whose lack of independence and impartiality has been established cannot, in any circumstances, guarantee a fair trial to the persons subject to its jurisdiction.
r0074: 38.  Having regard to its finding of a violation of Mr Özel’s right to have his case heard by an independent and impartial tribunal, the Court considers that it is unnecessary to examine this complaint (see, among other authorities, Çıraklar, cited above, p. 14, §§ 44-45).
r0075: II.  APPLICATION OF ARTICLE 41 OF THE CONVENTION
r0077: “If the Court finds that there has been a violation of the Convention or the Protocols thereto, and if the internal law of the High Contracting Party concerned allows only partial reparation to be made, the Court shall, if necessary, afford just satisfaction to the injured party.”
